Joint Exploratory Analysis — Cyclical Encoding Using Sine and Cosine

This analysis focuses exclusively on the joint relationship between the monthly cycle and the daily hourly cycle.

Monthly cycle: TRANS_MONTH_SIN + TRANS_MONTH_COS
Hourly cycle: TRANS_HOUR_SIN + TRANS_HOUR_COS

Total dataset observations: 1852394
Complete finite observations analyzed: 1852394
Excluded observations: 0
Excluded percentage: 0.000000%

1. Month × hour joint frequency

The original monthly and hourly positions are temporarily reconstructed from their sine and cosine components. Each observation is then assigned to one of 12 months and one of 24 hourly intervals. The original dataset is not modified.

3. Chi-square test of independence

H0: Month and hour are statistically independent.
H1: Month and hour are statistically associated.

Metric Value
Chi-square statistic 276.852432
Degrees of freedom 253
P-value 1.449858699329e-01
Alpha 0.05
Decision Fail to reject H0
Minimum expected frequency 3159.733996
Expected cells below 5 0
Expected cells below 5 (%) 0.000000%

The chi-square test does not reject the null hypothesis of independence between month and hour. The analysis does not provide sufficient statistical evidence of association at the selected significance level.

Because the dataset contains a very large number of observations, statistical significance can be detected even when the practical association is small. For this reason, the chi-square p-value should be interpreted together with Cramer's V.

4. Cramer's V

Cramer's V quantifies the magnitude of the association between month and hour. Its range is from 0 to 1.

Metric Value
Cramer's V 0.003686
Association strength Very weak or negligible
The strength labels used in this report are descriptive guidelines:

|V| < 0.10: Very weak or negligible
|V| < 0.30: Weak
|V| < 0.50: Moderate
|V| < 0.70: Strong
|V| ≥ 0.70: Very strong

These thresholds are descriptive and should not be interpreted as universal inferential cutoffs.

5. Adjusted standardized chi-square residuals

Adjusted standardized residuals identify the specific Month × Hour combinations that contribute most strongly to the departure from statistical independence.

Positive residuals indicate combinations observed more frequently than expected under independence. Negative residuals indicate combinations observed less frequently than expected.

Metric Value
Reference absolute residual threshold 2.00
Cells above expected threshold 10
Cells below expected threshold 7
Total notable cells 17
Notable cells (%) 5.902778%
Maximum positive residual 3.706881
Minimum negative residual -2.549203
An adjusted standardized residual close to zero indicates that the observed frequency is close to the value expected under independence.

Residual ≥ +2.0: the Month × Hour combination occurs notably more often than expected.
Residual ≤ -2.0: the Month × Hour combination occurs notably less often than expected.

The ±2.0 threshold is used as an exploratory reference rather than as a universal decision rule. Because multiple cells are examined simultaneously, these residuals should primarily be interpreted as exploratory diagnostics of the contingency table.

6. Circular-circular association

The Jammalamadaka-Sarma coefficient evaluates the association between the annual-cycle angle and the daily-cycle angle while preserving the circular nature of both variables.

Relationship Coefficient Direction Strength
Month angle × Hour angle 0.001070 Positive Very weak or negligible
This coefficient is more appropriate for the direct relationship between the two cyclical variables than treating reconstructed month and hour as ordinary continuous linear variables. The cyclical structure preserves boundaries such as December-to-January and 23:59-to-00:00.

7. Cross-cycle component correlations

Only relationships between the monthly cycle and the hourly cycle are evaluated here. The following within-cycle relationships are intentionally excluded:

  • TRANS_MONTH_SIN × TRANS_MONTH_COS
  • TRANS_HOUR_SIN × TRANS_HOUR_COS

Sine and cosine belonging to the same cyclical encoding jointly represent one variable and should not be interpreted as ordinary redundant features.

Exploratory conclusion:

This analysis focuses exclusively on the relationship between the monthly and hourly cyclical structures.

The joint frequency and conditional distributions describe how hourly transaction patterns vary across months.

The chi-square test evaluates whether the Month × Hour contingency structure departs from statistical independence.

Cramer's V quantifies the overall magnitude of that association.

Adjusted standardized residuals identify which specific Month × Hour combinations occur more or less frequently than expected under independence.

The Jammalamadaka-Sarma coefficient evaluates the relationship between the two cycles directly in angular space.

Pearson and Spearman correlations between cross-cycle sine and cosine components are reported as complementary descriptive measures.

No sine or cosine component is removed or classified as redundant during this analysis.
